Trader consensus on the 94–95°F and 96–97°F bins reflects this narrow uncertainty range, with lower probabilities assigned to extremes because climatological August maxima average 89–91°F and recent record heat on August 14 has not produced sustained conditions for 98°F-plus readings.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent MetService forecasts and model guidance indicate a high of 11°C for Wellington on August 18 under a showery south to southwest flow, with overnight lows near 6°C and gusty southerlies limiting daytime warming. This aligns with August climatology (typical maxima ~12°C) and recent polar-air intrusions that produced highs of 9–11°C. NIWA’s seasonal outlook assigns near-average temperatures the highest probability for the central North Island region, while persistent southerly advection and cloud cover suppress any significant rebound toward 13°C or above. Trader consensus at 62% for 11°C and 28.5% for 12°C therefore reflects the narrow forecast envelope, with only modest upside risk if the flow weakens or ridging develops ahead of the next front.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Marine layer and persistent onshore flow from the Pacific are capping maximum temperatures across Los Angeles on August 18, keeping the highest readings centered in the upper 70s to low 80s.** National Weather Service guidance shows coastal stations such as LAX forecast near 77–79°F under mostly sunny skies, while downtown areas may reach around 84°F before the sea breeze strengthens. This contrast produces the market’s heavy clustering on the 78–79°F (55%) and 80–81°F (23.5%) brackets, with 76–77°F also drawing notable support at 17.5%. 

Typical August climatology features average highs near 84°F downtown and lower values at the coast, but recent model consensus points to enhanced on-shore flow and a weak upper trough that limits daytime heating and prevents stronger offshore warming. These conditions align with observed recent days when coastal highs stayed in the mid- to upper 70s despite warmer inland readings. The implied probabilities therefore reflect traders incorporating the moderating influence of the marine environment and the latest forecast guidance rather than historical averages alone.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for the highest temperature in Karachi on August 19 centers on 32°C (51.5% implied probability) and 33°C (27.5%), reflecting typical monsoon-season conditions.** 

Pakistan Meteorological Department forecasts and model consensus indicate hot, humid weather with possible rain-wind or thundershowers, which increase cloud cover and reduce peak insolation, keeping maxima near the long-term August average of 31–32°C. Coastal sea breezes further moderate temperatures, while recent observations show daily highs fluctuating between 31–34°C amid variable monsoon moisture. These factors position 32°C as the mode, with slight upside risk to 33°C if clearer skies develop. New forecast updates from the PMD and global models over the next 48 hours will refine resolution probabilities around the 32–33°C threshold.

eventMetadata.context_description: The closely matched trader odds favoring 28–29°C for Manila’s August 19 high reflect the southwest monsoon’s ongoing suppression of daytime heating through persistent cloud cover and scattered rains across Luzon. Official PAGASA guidance shows forecast maxima of 29–31°C with 60% rain chances, consistent with recent observations of 27.8°C under similar conditions and climatological August averages near 30°C when monsoon flow intensifies. Reduced insolation and evaporative cooling from thunderstorms differentiate these lower outcomes from warmer scenarios, while model consensus on monsoon strength and steering patterns limits upside potential. Updated PAGASA briefings and next model runs will clarify whether localized clearing allows brief spikes toward 30°C or maintains the cooler bias.
